sentences.text: Ctenacanthus belongs to the class Chondrichthyes, a group of cartilaginous fish, and is placed in the family Ctenacanthidae.
Fossils of Ctenacanthus have been discovered in the Bloyd Formation of Arkansas and the Cleveland Shale of Ohio, as well as in South America.
The genus Ctenacanthus was first described by Louis Agassiz in 1837.
Analysis of tooth wear in Ctenacanthus concinnus suggests it was an opportunistic feeder that consumed various prey, including other cartilaginous fish and ectocochleate cephalopods.
This animal lived from the Emsian to the Changhsingian stages, spanning approximately 410.62 to 251.902 million years ago.
